project.name: cavet
project.description: A Go CLI security-triage tool for coding agents. It runs scanners (trivy, opengrep, gitleaks, checkov) inside an offline container engine and records every finding and decision in an append-only audit log.
project.context: This finding comes from a scan of the cavet repository itself.

finding.description:
engine/Dockerfile:171
Multiple ENTRYPOINT instructions were found. Only the last one will take effect.
verdict: dismissed (high confidence, by operator): the two ENTRYPOINT instructions sit in separate final stages (final-core at line 155, final-full at line 171, each FROM rules); each stage has exactly one effective entrypoint, the rule cannot see stage boundaries

mechanical_context.path_class: container image build definition (shipped as the scanner engine image)
mechanical_context.source_excerpt:
141 | FROM rules AS final-core
  142 | COPY --from=trivy-data-core /opt/trivy-cache /opt/trivy-cache
  143 | COPY entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/cavet-entrypoint.sh
  144 | COPY healthcheck     /usr/local/bin/cavet-healthcheck
  145 | COPY gitleaks.toml   /opt/gitleaks.toml
  146 | COPY LICENSES.md     /LICENSES.md
  147 | RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/cavet-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/cavet-healthcheck
  148 | 
  149 | # engine-spec §6.3: CLI passes --user uid:gid on Linux hosts; arbitrary uids
  150 | # need a writable HOME (git config --global) and pre-existing scratch dirs
  151 | # (entrypoint mkdir -p must no-op, not create). Root default is unaffected.
  152 | ENV HOME=/tmp
  153 | RUN mkdir -p /reports /scan && chmod 0777 /reports /scan
